findings.summary: `unmodeled_markdown` never checks the config pairs' `docs` globs, so an explicitly paired spec that lives in a docs-only directory is reported as unmodeled — contradicting INV-8's "no file is ever both unmodeled and paired".
findings.evidence: Doc INV-8: "Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired." Doc §2 defines Pair as "`{label, code[], docs[]}` — links code globs to spec doc(s)." Code (unmodeled_markdown) filters only on three conditions: `if d in code_dirs: continue` / `if classify_exclude(md, user_excludes) == "user": continue` / `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue` — `pair_docs` is not passed in and is only computed later, inside `coverage()` for the orphan check (`if md in pair_docs: continue  # explicitly paired — governed, wherever its code is`). So with `pairs: [{code: [src/*.py], docs: [docs/a-spec.md]}, …]` and 3+ such specs under `docs/`, those paired docs land in `unmodeled` as "outside the same-stem pairing model" while their code is simultaneously counted as covered.
findings.suggestion: Either pass `pair_docs` into `unmodeled_markdown` and skip pair-declared docs the same way the orphan check does, or reword INV-8 to drop the "never both unmodeled and paired" clause (e.g. "…so an unmodeled file never has a same-stem code sibling; explicitly pair-declared docs may still appear").

verification.doc_quote: | INV-8 | Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired. |
verification.why: The invariants table asserts, in the exact universal strength the finding needs, that no file is ever both unmodeled and paired, and `Pair` is defined in §2 as carrying `docs[]`, so an explicitly paired doc in a docs-only tree landing in `unmodeled` contradicts a normative rule that no other passage corrects.

findings.summary: The doc names an agent skill's `SKILL.md` as a body of writing the unmodeled report surfaces, but `skill` is in `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS`, so every `SKILL.md` is filtered out before grouping.
findings.evidence: Doc §3 (Unmodeled markdown detection, Why): "two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references)". Code: `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS = {"readme", …, "skill", …}` and in `unmodeled_markdown`: `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue  # README/CHANGELOG/… are docs, not an unmodeled corpus`. A repo of three skills, each `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with no reference files, therefore reports an empty `unmodeled` list — the exact 0%-but-thoroughly-specified case the section claims to name. (AC-4 works only because it uses `reference.md`.)
findings.suggestion: Either drop `"skill"` from `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS` for the unmodeled path (keeping it for the orphan path), or amend the doc to say only a skill's *reference* markdown is surfaced because `SKILL.md` is treated as a conventional doc name.

verification.doc_quote: **Why:** two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references).
verification.why: The cited line is explicitly "Why:" rationale explaining what the same-stem pairing model cannot reach — motivation for the section rather than a claim that `unmodeled_markdown` reports `SKILL.md` files (the normative behavior is the three-condition sentence above it and AC-4).

findings.summary: The §2 glossary defines UNMODELED by "no code sibling", but the code qualifies a file by "its directory holds no candidate code file" — a stricter condition that §3 states correctly.
findings.evidence: Doc §2: "UNMODELED | A directory tree of at least 3 markdown files that same-stem pairing cannot reach — no code sibling, not a conventional doc." Code: `code_dirs = {os.path.dirname(rel) for rel in candidate}` … `if d in code_dirs: continue  # sits beside code — the pairing model already sees it`. Given `src/a.py` plus `src/x.md`, `src/y.md`, `src/z.md` (none with a same-stem `.py`), the glossary predicts an unmodeled group of 3; the code reports none (they go to `orphans` instead).
findings.suggestion: Change the §2 row to match §3: "…markdown in a directory that holds no candidate code file, not a conventional doc."

verification.doc_quote: A file qualifies when it sits in a directory holding no candidate code, is not user-excluded, and is not a conventional doc name.
verification.why: §3 states the qualifying rule exactly as implemented (directory holding no candidate code), and INV-8 repeats it, so the loose glossary phrasing does not make the document wrong.
